notes.title: Web-searched & fact-checked
notes.body: Every place is traceable to a credible source — Michelin, UNESCO, local news & magazines, and vetted local/viral creators — in data/sources.json. Coordinates are verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open. Yelp/TripAdvisor never count toward the two-source bar.

places.ad: 135 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The modernist 1960s presidential palace where NVA Tank 843 crashed the gate on 30 April 1975, ending the war. Frozen-in-time state rooms, war-command bunker and telecoms basement. National monument; daily ~07:00-18:00, 80,000d.

places.ad: 01 Cong xa Paris, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The twin-spired red-brick French cathedral (1863-1880) built with imported Marseille materials, on the square opposite the Post Office. UNDER RESTORATION since 2017 (interior closed to visitors; completion pushed to ~2027, scaffolding coming off by early 2026) — view the exterior.

places.ad: 125 Cong xa Paris (Hai Ba Trung), Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Working 1886-1891 post office (architect Alfred Foulhoux; often mis-credited to Eiffel) with a vaulted iron-truss hall, painted maps and a portrait of Ho Chi Minh. Ranked among the world's most beautiful post offices; still operational.

places.ad: 73 Mai Thi Luu, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Saigon's most atmospheric Taoist temple, built by the Cantonese community in 1909, thick with incense smoke and carved wooden deities incl. the Hall of Ten Hells and a turtle pond. Obama visited in 2016. Free, ~07:00-18:00.

places.n: Nguyen Hue Walking Street & People's Committee Building
places.ad: Nguyen Hue Boulevard, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The city's 900 m pedestrian boulevard (a former canal, walkerised 2015) running from the floodlit French Hotel de Ville / People's Committee Building (1898-1909, viewed from outside) and Ho Chi Minh statue down to the Saigon River. Liveliest at night.

places.ad: 07 Cong Truong Lam Son, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Flamboyant 1897-1900 French Beaux-Arts theatre, once seat of South Vietnam's Lower House, now a national relic staging the acclaimed bamboo-circus A O Show and The Mist.

places.ad: 36 Ho Tung Mau, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The 262 m lotus-bud tower (2010) with a helipad wing and the 49th-floor Saigon Skydeck, the city's first observation deck, giving 360-degree views over the river. Open daily ~09:30-21:30.

places.n: Ho Chi Minh City Museum (Gia Long Palace)
places.ad: 65 Ly Tu Trong, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: City-history museum in an 1885-1890 neoclassical palace that served the French governor, President Diem (as Gia Long Palace) and the RVN Supreme Court, with a wartime bunker/tunnel beneath. Traces Saigon from prehistory to reunification.

places.ad: 2 Nguyen Binh Khiem, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Vietnam's national-history collection in a 1926-1929 Indochinese-style building beside the Botanical Gardens: Cham and Oc Eo antiquities, Dong Son drums, a mummified noblewoman, plus water-puppet shows. Closed Mondays.

places.n: Fine Arts Museum (Bao tang My thuat)
places.ad: 97A Pho Duc Chinh, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The city's leading art museum in a yellow 1929-1934 Franco-Chinese mansion of the wealthy Hua family, with the first lift in Saigon; holds lacquer, silk and war-era painting plus Champa/Oc Eo relics. Closed Mondays.

places.ad: 42 Nguyen Hue, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A crumbling 1960s nine-storey block (once housing for US advisers) reborn as a vertical warren of independent cafes, boutiques and bars, each balcony overlooking the walking street. Slow lift ~3,000d, or take the stairs.

places.ad: Bui Vien Street, Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Saigon's neon backpacker strip in the Pham Ngu Lao quarter (on the map since Lonely Planet's 1993 guide) — bar stools spilling into the road, street food and live music. Pedestrianised nightly; peaks Fri-Sun.

places.n: Ho Chi Minh Museum - Dragon House Wharf (Nha Rong)
places.ad: 1 Nguyen Tat Thanh, District 4, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The 1862-1863 twin-dragon-roofed former Messageries Maritimes house on the riverfront from which the 21-year-old future Ho Chi Minh sailed to France in June 1911; a branch of the Ho Chi Minh Museum since 1979. Closed Mondays.

places.ad: Cong Truong Quoc Te (Pham Ngoc Thach / Tran Cao Van), District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A modernist 1967-1972 traffic-circle monument of five splayed concrete 'hands' and an octagonal fountain, on the site of a French water tower and an old Nguyen-era citadel gate. Now a beloved evening hangout for street snacks.

places.ad: 202 Vo Thi Sau, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A 31,000-object museum (est. 1985; Class-I museum from 2024) devoted to southern Vietnamese women in war and culture — female guerrillas, ao dai history and Mother Goddess worship. Closed Mondays; free.

places.ad: 5 Ton Duc Thang, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Riverside museum (opened 1988) to Ton Duc Thang, Vietnam's second president and a Con Dao political prisoner, with 16,000+ documents on his life and the labour movement. Closed Mondays; free.

places.ad: 104 Yersin, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The 'American Market' off Yersin St, famous since 1975 for army-surplus gear, dog tags, ponchos and militaria (genuine and replica) alongside hardware stalls — a gritty relic of the war years. Bargain and check provenance.

places.ad: 339 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia, Ward 7, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The city's largest Mahayana pagoda (built 1964-1971 with Japanese aid), the first to render traditional temple form in concrete, crowned by a seven-storey, 40 m stupa. Free.

places.ad: 89 Ba Huyen Thanh Quan, Vo Thi Sau Ward, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A seven-storey 1956-1958 pagoda that was the flashpoint of the 1963 Buddhist Crisis: the epicentre of anti-Diem protests and the 21 August 1963 army raid that arrested hundreds of monks and helped trigger the coup.

places.ad: 289 Hai Ba Trung, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The bubblegum-pink Romano-Gothic Catholic church begun 1870-1876 (its signature pink dates to a 1957 repaint) — the city's second-largest church and a landmark photo stop. Active parish; exterior always, interior around Mass times.

places.ad: 720A Dien Bien Phu, Ward 22, Binh Thanh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: At 461 m the tallest building in Vietnam (2018), a bamboo-cluster supertall over the Saigon River in Vinhomes Central Park. The SkyView observatory spans floors 79-81 for the city's highest panorama.

places.ad: 710 Nguyen Trai, Ward 11, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Cholon's most famous temple (Tue Thanh Guildhall), built by Cantonese immigrants around 1760 for Mazu, sea goddess of the overseas Chinese. Famed for its porcelain-figurine roof friezes and hanging incense coils. National monument.

places.ad: 57A Thap Muoi, Ward 2, District 6 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Cholon's grand wholesale market, financed by merchant Quach Dam and completed 1928, built around a pagoda-roofed courtyard; a recognised heritage building (restored 2016-2018) and still a major distribution hub.

places.ad: 25 Hoc Lac, Ward 14, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Cholon's Chinese-Catholic parish church (1900-1902), Gothic with Chinese detailing. Here President Ngo Dinh Diem and his brother took refuge and surrendered during the 1 November 1963 coup, before being killed en route.

places.ad: 678 Nguyen Trai, Ward 11, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A 19th-century Teochew guildhall temple to the deified warlord Quan Cong, one of Cholon's oldest, celebrated for its gilded woodwork, a huge red-lacquer horse of Quan Cong and intricate roof ceramics.

places.ad: 802 Nguyen Trai, Ward 14, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A southern-Fujian (Zhangzhou) guildhall temple founded 1809 for Thien Hau, with four China-carved dragon-wrapped stone pillars shipped in by boat and vivid ceramic roof scenes; especially alive at the Lantern Festival.

places.ad: 565 Lac Long Quan, Ward 10, Tan Binh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Believed the oldest temple in the city (founded 1744), atmospheric in garden grounds with a Bodhi tree, a nine-tier stupa and thousands of decorative plates set into its walls. National relic. Free.

places.ad: Long Hoa, Hoa Thanh, Tay Ninh Province, Vietnam (day trip ~90 km NW of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
places.w: The kaleidoscopic 1933-1955 Great Temple of Caodaism, Vietnam's homegrown syncretic religion, with a divine 'all-seeing eye', dragon pillars and rainbow interior. Time a visit for the white-robed noon ceremony. Often paired with Cu Chi.

places.n: Mekong Delta Day Trip (My Tho & Ben Tre)
places.ad: My Tho (Tien Giang) & Ben Tre Provinces, Vietnam (day trip ~70-90 km SW of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
places.w: The classic close Delta day trip: a Tien River cruise past the Dragon/Unicorn/Phoenix/Tortoise islets, sampan rides through coconut-palm canals, a coconut-candy workshop, honey tea and the large Vinh Trang Pagoda at My Tho.

places.ad: Ninh Son, Tay Ninh Province, Vietnam (day trip ~100 km NW of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
places.w: The 986 m 'Black Virgin Mountain', highest peak in the south, a pilgrimage site of cave temples reached by a Guinness-record cable-car system to Sun World, with a 72 m bronze Bodhisattva at the summit. Pairs with Tay Ninh's Cao Dai temple.

places.n: Can Gio Mangrove Biosphere Reserve (Monkey Island)
places.ad: Can Gio District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (~50-60 km SE of the centre)
places.w: Vietnam's first UNESCO Man-and-Biosphere reserve (designated 2000), a replanted mangrove forest that was the Viet Cong's Rung Sac guerrilla zone. Boat trips, a reconstructed guerrilla base, crocodile lagoons and a large troop of macaques ('Monkey Island').

places.ad: Cai Rang District, Can Tho, Mekong Delta, Vietnam (long day trip / overnight ~170 km SW of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
places.w: The biggest floating wholesale market in the Delta, where boats trade produce hung from tall poles at dawn on the Can Tho River. Deep in the Delta (~3.5 hrs each way) — best as an early-start long day trip or overnight; trades wind down by ~08:30.

places.ad: Ha Long St, Ward 2, Vung Tau, Ba Ria-Vung Tau Province, Vietnam (day trip ~95 km / 2-hr ferry from Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
places.w: The nearest beach escape: a seaside town crowned by a 32 m Christ the King statue (1974) you can climb (~800 steps inside) for coastal views, plus the White Palace and Back Beach. Reachable by road or Saigon River fast ferry.

places.ad: 45 Truong Dinh, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Saigon's only Hindu temple, a vivid South-Indian shrine built by Tamil merchants in the late 1800s to the goddess Mariamman, its ~12 m gopuram crowded with painted deities. Free; daily ~07:00-19:00, remove shoes.

places.ad: Truong Dinh Street, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: One of central Saigon's largest green spaces (a former French garden), with a Cham-style shrine, a Hung Kings temple and a famous early-morning 'bird cafe' where locals hang songbird cages (~06:00-09:00; disrupted in recent years by Metro works). Free.

places.ad: 81 Nguyen Xien, Long Binh Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A gleaming white Thai/Indian-style Theravada temple and 56 m Gotama Cetiya stupa on a hill above the Dong Nai River in Thu Duc, named by National Geographic (2019) among the world's 10 most beautiful Buddhist sites. Free; incense-free grounds.

places.ad: 1147 Binh Quoi, Ward 28 (Thanh Da Peninsula), Binh Thanh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A riverside 'traditional-village' recreation park on the Thanh Da peninsula run by Saigontourist, known for its weekend Southern-style buffets, folk games and thatched-hut gardens along the Saigon River. Free entry; paid activities and buffet.

places.ad: 244 Ba Tháng Hai, Ward 12, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A landmark District 10 Buddhist temple on Ba Tháng Hai (3/2) Boulevard, originally built in 1964 and rebuilt 2014–2017 around a soaring 13-storey stupa (Tháp Đa Bảo). A historically significant seat of Vietnamese Buddhism and a striking, uncrowded stop; upper floors open on the 1st and 15th of the lunar month.

places.ad: 24 Chánh Hưng, Ward 4, District 8, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A near-180-year-old Buddhist temple in District 8 whose surfaces are almost entirely mosaicked in over 30 tonnes of broken porcelain and ceramic shards — bowls, plates, teapots — applied by hand from 1961 to 2004. Holds a Vietnam Book of Records mark for the most ceramic pieces, plus a pair of 3.4 m, 1.8-tonne candles. The 'Miểng Sành' pagoda is District 8's signature sight.

places.n: Bến Bình Đông & the Tết Flower Market
places.ad: Bến Bình Đông (along Kênh Tàu Hủ), Ward 11, District 8, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The old rice-trade wharf strung along Kênh Tàu Hủ, once the 'prosperous Tàu Hủ avenue' linking Saigon-Chợ Lớn to the Mekong. Each Lunar New Year it becomes the 'trên bến dưới thuyền' flower market, with growers selling blooms straight off sampans — the most atmospheric Tết scene in the city and a working glimpse of canal-borne Saigon.

places.ad: Cầu Nhị Thiên Đường (over Kênh Đôi), Ward 5, District 8, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A 1925 bridge over the Kênh Đôi, said to be the first reinforced-concrete bridge in Indochina, built by the Chinese-Vietnamese magnate behind the Nhị Thiên Đường medicated-oil empire. A row of arches beneath it evokes an old Roman viaduct; a District 8 landmark and marker of the Nam Bộ resistance era.

places.ad: 1 Đường số 17A, Bình Trị Đông B Ward, Bình Tân, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The 114,000 sqm Japanese-run mall that anchors Bình Tân, opened 2016 as one of the largest in Ho Chi Minh City — cinema, a huge food street, and the everyday air-conditioned pull for the district's working-class west. The practical family day-out landmark out here.

places.n: Bà Điểm & the Eighteen Betel Garden Villages (18 Thôn Vườn Trầu)
places.ad: Bà Điểm Commune, Hóc Môn, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The historic areca-and-betel-growing belt around Bà Điểm, famed since the 18th century and a cradle of the 1940 Southern Uprising — the Southern Party Committee sheltered in its gardens. Today a living cultural-heritage landscape of remnant trầu (betel) gardens and revolutionary memory rather than a ticketed attraction.

places.ad: 30 Bờ Bao Tân Thắng, Sơn Kỳ Ward, Tân Phú, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: AEON's first shopping mall in Vietnam, opened 11 Jan 2014 — a ~70,000 m² Japanese-anchored complex in the Celadon City estate that made Vietnam the third country (after Malaysia and China) with a large-scale AEON MALL. A CGV cinema, food court, indoor playground and 200+ brands make it the western suburbs' main weekend gathering place.

places.ad: 120 Hanoi Highway, Tan Phu Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The world's first Buddhism-themed amusement/water park (opened 1995), a surreal 200-ha spread of giant dragons, a neon-haloed Buddha shrine, a 'Buddhist Hell' walkthrough and waterslides pouring from sages' beards. ~1.5-2M visitors/year; daily ~07:30-17:00. Reachable on Metro Line 1.

places.n: Vietnam National Historical Culture Park (Cong vien Lich su Van hoa Dan toc)
places.ad: Long Binh Ward, Thu Duc (District 9), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A ~400-ha state park recreating Vietnam's history in themed zones, anchored by the grand Hung Kings temple complex where the city holds its official Hung Kings' Death Anniversary rites. Long-running build-out; the ancient/Hung-Kings zone is the finished, visit-worthy core.

places.n: Crescent Mall & Starlight Bridge (Cau Anh Sao)
places.ad: Ton Dat Tien, Phu My Hung, District 7, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The centrepiece of planned Phu My Hung: a 170 m LED-lit pedestrian bridge over crescent-shaped Ho Ban Nguyet lake, glowing like a starry sky at night, beside the riverfront Crescent Mall. The go-to evening promenade of Saigon's affluent south.

places.ad: Vinh Cuu District, Tri An, Dong Nai, Vietnam
places.w: Vietnam's largest man-made reservoir (behind the Tri An hydro dam), a vast expanse dotted with ~76 forested islets, popular for boat trips, sunrise/sunset floats, island picnics and overnight fishing with local boatmen. ~65-70 km northeast of HCMC.

places.n: Dai Nam Wonderland (Dai Nam Van Hien)
places.ad: Dai Nam, Thu Dau Mot, Binh Duong, Vietnam
places.w: Vietnam's largest tourist complex (711 ha, opened 2008): an amusement park, a man-made 'sea' with wave beach, a zoo/safari, a racecourse and the colossal gilded Kim Dien (Dai Nam) temple, once the country's biggest. ~40 km north of HCMC.

places.ad: Hai Dang, Ward 2 (Nui Nho), Vung Tau, Vietnam
places.w: Built by the French in 1862, the oldest of Vietnam's ~79 lighthouses, perched atop Nui Nho (Small Mountain); a short climb up 55 steps delivers a 360-degree view over the city, harbour and the Christ statue on the opposite hill.

places.ad: Thuy Van, Bai Sau, Vung Tau, Vietnam
places.w: Vung Tau's main swimming beach, a ~10 km southeast-facing strand lined with loungers, seafood shacks and water sports (surf, SUP, kite-surf); the Saigonese weekend seaside default, two hours from the city.

places.ad: Nguyen Trung Truc, My Phong, My Tho, Tien Giang, Vietnam
places.w: The largest and most famous pagoda in Tien Giang (completed 1850), a national heritage site blending Vietnamese, Khmer, Chinese and European arches, set in gardens with giant Buddha statues; the standout stop on any My Tho / Mekong day trip.

places.n: Sun World Ba Đen Mountain Cable Car
places.ad: Sun World Ba Den Mountain, Núi Bà Đen, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
places.w: The Doppelmayr cable-car complex that lifts you up the 986 m 'Roof of the South' in minutes instead of a three-hour climb. Its Ba Den departure station holds the Guinness World Record for the largest cable-car station (10,959 sqm), moving 4,400 passengers an hour to the spiritual complex on top.

places.n: Tây Bổ Đà Sơn Buddha Statue
places.ad: Summit of Núi Bà Đen, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
places.w: A 72 m bronze Bodhisattva cast from 170+ tonnes of red copper on the 986 m summit — recognised by Guinness as Asia's tallest bronze Lady-Buddha statue on a mountain peak. Ringed by terraced gardens and often wrapped in cloud, it is the visual icon of the Bà Đen complex.

places.ad: Dầu Tiếng, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
places.w: Vietnam and Southeast Asia's largest artificial lake — 270 sqkm damming the upper Saigon River, completed 1985 — now an ecotourism draw of forested islets and hill-fringed water. A go-to for camping, fishing and sunset-watching on the far side of Bà Đen.

places.ad: Long Hoa, Hòa Thành, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
places.w: Tây Ninh's busiest market, laid out in 1952 to the design of Cao Đài dignitary Phạm Công Tắc to serve the faith's followers. The place to buy the province's edible souvenirs — dew-soaked rice paper, muối tôm, sesame and beans — and to eat at its famous vegetarian stalls.

places.ad: off Mũi Nghinh Phong / Bãi Sau, Phường 2, Vũng Tàu, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
places.w: A tiny rocky islet crowned by a small temple locals hold sacred; at low tide a natural stone causeway surfaces so you can walk out from the shore. A quiet sunrise and spiritual spot — time it carefully or the rising tide strands you.

places.ad: Quang Trung / Trần Phú promenade, Bãi Trước, Vũng Tàu, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
places.w: Vũng Tàu's crescent-bay waterfront between Big and Small Mountain — a palm-lined promenade for sunset strolls, seafood and coconuts, ringed by landmarks (Bạch Dinh, the cable-car station, Phước Thắng Fortress). The city's social heart, quieter than Back Beach.

places.n: Nhà Lớn Long Sơn (Đền Ông Trần)
places.ad: Long Sơn commune (Núi Nứa island), Vũng Tàu, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
places.w: A one-of-a-kind 2-hectare wood-and-tile temple compound on Long Sơn island, built 1910–1929 by Lê Văn Mưu ('Ông Trần'), founder of a local folk faith blending Confucianism and Taoism. Temple, mausoleum and communal halls with a century-old tamarind tree; a national relic and the island's living heritage site.

places.n: Bình Châu Hot Springs (Suối khoáng nóng Bình Châu)
places.ad: Bình Châu, Xuyên Mộc, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
places.w: Southern Vietnam's only natural hot mineral springs — 70-plus surface vents from 37°C up to a boiling 82°C, set in the Bình Châu–Phước Bửu coastal forest with soaking pools, mud baths and an egg-boiling spring. A classic overnight on the Hồ Tràm–Hồ Cốc coast road.

places.ad: Hồ Tràm, Phước Thuận, Xuyên Mộc, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
places.w: A long, quiet arc of fine sand and clear water between Long Hải and Bình Châu, ~125 km from HCMC — casuarina-lined, cheap seafood at the fishing hamlet, and the anchor of the coast's cluster of beach resorts and golf courses. With Hồ Cốc, the best beach within easy reach of Saigon.

places.ad: Bình Châu / Bưng Riềng, Xuyên Mộc, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
places.w: An 11,293-hectare protected coastal rainforest — the region's only surviving lowland dipterocarp forest — wrapping the Hồ Tràm and Hồ Cốc beaches and the Bình Châu hot springs. Home to the 136m Núi Hồ Linh hill and endangered species; hiking trails through a rare intact ecosystem.

places.ad: 870 Truong Sa, Ward 14, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A near-century-old pagoda on the Nhieu Loc Canal, a city-designated heritage site and the city's most photogenic Vesak venue, when thousands of lanterns are floated on the water. Serene canal-side visit any day; spectacular at Buddha's Birthday (4th lunar month).

places.ad: 1408 Duong 3 Thang 2, Ward 2, District 11, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: An early-19th-century pagoda built on the foundations of an ancient Khmer/Oc Eo-era temple mound, a recognised National Historical-Cultural Monument with a fine timber-framed Southern-style hall. A quiet, deeply historic stop in District 11.

places.ad: Pham Ngu Lao, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A long, 9-hectare downtown green ribbon on the site of Saigon's demolished 19th-century railway station, running from behind Ben Thanh Market through the backpacker quarter. Handy central breathing space for a stroll or people-watching.

places.ad: Dien Bien Phu, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A shaded central park laid out in 1983 over the former Massiges (European) Cemetery, once the resting place of colonial elites and President Ngo Dinh Diem. A leafy escape with a fascinating buried history documented by Saigoneer.

places.ad: 10B Ton Duc Thang, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The 1.3 km riverside park and pier on the Saigon River where locals gather at sunset and river cruises and the 15,000d public waterbus depart for Thu Duc. The best way to see the city from the water, past Landmark 81 and Bitexco.

places.ad: 55B Nguyen Thi Minh Khai, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The city's main venue for mua roi nuoc (water puppetry), the thousand-year-old northern folk art performed on a pool of water with live traditional musicians. Two short shows daily (17:00 and 18:30) beside Tao Dan Park.

places.ad: 132-134 Dong Khoi, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The city's oldest hotel (1880) on former Rue Catinat opposite the Opera House, where Graham Greene wrote much of 'The Quiet American' in Room 214 and its terrace was the correspondents' 1950s watering hole. A living piece of literary and war-era Saigon.

places.ad: 01 Dong Khoi, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A 1925 French-colonial landmark on the Dong Khoi/Ton Duc Thang riverfront corner, built by the tycoon Hui Bon Hoa and preserving its original Art Deco character. Worth a look for the facade and a drink at its river-view rooftop.

places.ad: 141 Nguyen Hue, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The open-air rooftop bar of the 1960 Rex Hotel, site of the US military's daily wartime press briefings mocked as the 'Five O'Clock Follies'. Iconic Vietnam-War history plus sweeping views over Nguyen Hue and City Hall.

places.ad: 65 Le Loi, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The city's most polished shopping complex on Le Loi, anchored by Vietnam's first Takashimaya Japanese department store with a top-floor food court and basement Japanese supermarket. A cool, glossy contrast to the street markets.

places.ad: 3 Hoa Binh, Ward 3, District 11, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A 50-hectare cultural-and-amusement park in District 11 with landscaped gardens, thrill rides, cultural exhibits and an adjoining water park. One of the city's big family day-outs, alongside Suoi Tien and Dai Nam.

places.ad: Xã Tân Hiệp, huyện Hóc Môn, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Founded 1957 on ~6 ha in suburban Hóc Môn, this is regarded as the largest Buddhist practice-and-teaching center in Vietnam, with 50+ affiliated branches. Famous for its mass seven-day meditation retreats and student/summer courses; on Vu Lan and Tết it draws enormous crowds. Northern-Buddhist double-tiered tile roofs and a serene bougainvillea-lined forecourt.

places.n: Chùa núi Châu Thới (Chau Thoi Mountain Temple)
places.ad: Phường Bình An, TP. Dĩ An, Bình Dương, Vietnam
places.w: The oldest temple in Bình Dương (founded 1612) and one of the earliest in the whole south, perched atop an 82 m granite hill reached by a 220-step stone stair. A national scenic-landmark since 1989, with a 'sacred rock', panoramic views over the Đồng Nai plain and coiled-dragon rooflines — an easy ~40-minute pilgrimage day-trip from the city.

places.ad: Phường Phú Cường, TP. Thủ Dầu Một, Bình Dương, Vietnam
places.w: A near-300-year-old temple (founded 1741) in Thủ Dầu Một crowned by a 52 m-long, 12 m-high reclining Buddha completed in 2013 and recognized by Asia Records as the longest rooftop nirvana Buddha in Asia — set 23 m up on the roof, with 20 relief panels of the Buddha's life below. A serene old-Bình Dương compound of carved wood and lacquer.

places.ad: Nối Quận 1 với TP. Thủ Đức (sông Sài Gòn), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The city's newest icon — a cable-stayed bridge with a single soaring pylon, opened April 2022, linking central District 1 (Mê Linh Square) to the Thủ Thiêm new-urban area. Its artistic night lighting and the riverside park beneath it have made it one of Saigon's most popular sunset and check-in spots on the water.

places.ad: Nối Quận 1 với Quận 4 (kênh Bến Nghé), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: One of Saigon's oldest surviving bridges — a 128 m green iron arch built 1893–94 by Levallois-Perret (the old Eiffel firm) over the Bến Nghé canal, sibling in age to Hanoi's Long Biên. The French called it 'Arc-en-ciel' (rainbow); locals named it Cầu Mống for its arch. Ranked among the city's 10 heritage sites in 2015; a quiet evening photo spot.

places.n: Vườn quốc gia Cát Tiên (Cat Tien National Park)
places.ad: Huyện Tân Phú, Đồng Nai, Vietnam
places.w: A 70,000+ ha tropical-forest reserve and UNESCO World Biosphere ~150 km from the city — the region's marquee nature trip. The Nam Cát Tiên sector holds the trekking trails, Crocodile Lake (Bàu Sấu), the 400-year Tung tree, night wildlife spotting, gibbons and the Dao Tien primate centre. Best in the December–May dry season.

places.n: Đền thờ Trần Hưng Đạo (Tran Hung Dao Temple)
places.ad: 36 Võ Thị Sáu, phường Tân Định, Quận 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A dignified 1932/1958 temple to the national hero Trần Hưng Đạo on a quiet Tân Định block, built by the Bắc Việt mutual-aid society. Curved-tile roofs with dragon-and-phoenix motifs and a triple gate; ranked a city relic, and busiest around the eighth-lunar-month death anniversary of Đức Thánh Trần.

places.n: Tu viện Khánh An (Khanh An Monastery)
places.ad: 1055/3D Quốc lộ 1A, phường An Phú Đông, Quận 12, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A century-old monastery rebuilt over ~10 years (reopened 2016) in a serene Japanese-influenced style — timber and wood-grained structures in white, ochre and red-brown among green courtyards, earning it the nickname 'little Japan' of Saigon. A calm, camera-ready riverside retreat in District 12, busiest on weekends and full-moon days.

places.n: Công viên Lê Thị Riêng (Le Thi Rieng Park)
places.ad: 875 Cách Mạng Tháng Tám, Quận 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A green, lake-dotted culture park on Cách Mạng Tháng Tám — built in 1983 on the cleared Chí Hòa cemetery — that doubles as a family playground with the 'Thỏ Trắng' rides, pool, weekend magic shows and street-food stalls. Free entry; a local weekend hangout rather than a headline sight.

places.n: Bảo tàng Chiến dịch Hồ Chí Minh (Ho Chi Minh Campaign Museum)
places.ad: 2 Lê Duẩn, Quận 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A free military museum set in an early-20th-century French building beside Reunification Palace, opened 1987, devoted to the 1975 Spring Offensive that ended in the fall of Saigon. Maps, sand-table dioramas, weapons and photographs trace the final campaign; a focused complement to the nearby palace and War Remnants Museum.

places.n: Công viên Gia Định (Gia Dinh Park)
places.ad: Đường Hoàng Minh Giám, Quận Gò Vấp, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The largest green space in the city — a ~32 ha park at the meeting point of Gò Vấp, Tân Bình and Phú Nhuận with ~1,000 trees, 63,000 m² of lawn and a big children's play zone, split into Gia Định 1 and 2. The 'green lung' of Saigon: shaded jogging paths, picnics and early-morning tai chi.

places.n: Làng sơn mài Tương Bình Hiệp (Tuong Binh Hiep Lacquer Village)
places.ad: Phường Tương Bình Hiệp, TP. Thủ Dầu Một, Bình Dương, Vietnam
places.w: The near-300-year cradle of Bình Dương's fine-art lacquerware, recognized in 2016 as a National Intangible Cultural Heritage. Family workshops still build up gold-leaf and inlay lacquer over many painstaking layers; a living craft-village visit ~30 km from the city, best paired with Thủ Dầu Một's temples.

places.n: Làng bưởi Tân Triều (Tan Trieu Pomelo Village)
places.ad: Cù lao Tân Triều, xã Tân Bình, huyện Vĩnh Cửu, Đồng Nai, Vietnam
places.w: A river islet ~40 km from the city famed for its 'orange-leaf' pomelos — thin-skinned, sweet, faintly bitter aftertaste. A model community farm-tourism village where you pick fruit in the orchards and eat a whole pomelo-themed menu (pomelo salad, pomelo wine); Đồng Nai is developing it as a signature agri-tourism destination.

places.n: Tuyến Metro số 1 Bến Thành - Suối Tiên (Metro Line 1)
places.ad: Tuyến Bến Thành (Quận 1) – Suối Tiên (TP. Thủ Đức), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The city's first metro, opened 22 December 2024 after more than a decade of building — and an instant 'triệu-like' check-in phenomenon in its own right. The Bến Thành underground hall's lotus-shaped skylight and the elevated An Phú and Thảo Điền stations (sunset views over Thủ Đức) are the most-photographed spots; ride it as an attraction, not just transport.

places.n: Núi Chứa Chan & Chùa Gia Lào (Chua Chan Mountain)
places.ad: Huyện Xuân Lộc, Đồng Nai, Vietnam
places.w: At 837 m the second-highest peak in the south after Bà Đen — a national historical-scenic site (2012) and Đồng Nai's premier day-hike. Trek or take the cable car up through cloud-hunting viewpoints to the cliff-set Chùa Gia Lào (Bửu Quang) tucked under a giant three-trunk fig; camping on the summit is popular with young hikers ~110 km from the city.

places.n: Nhà thờ Đa Minh - Ba Chuông (Ba Chuong Church)
places.ad: 190 Lê Văn Sỹ, Quận Phú Nhuận, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A remarkable 1962 Catholic church on Lê Văn Sỹ that fuses East-Asian temple form with Christian meaning — its three-tiered bell tower and roofline echo a southern Vietnamese communal house (đình), with dragons turned to face the cross, and a square-nave/round-sanctuary plan symbolizing earth and heaven. One of the most architecturally distinctive churches in the city.

places.n: Đình Minh Hương Gia Thạnh (Minh Huong Gia Thanh Communal House)
places.ad: 380 Trần Hưng Đạo B, Quận 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The first communal house of the Chinese-Vietnamese (Minh Hương) community in Saigon-Chợ Lớn, built 1789 and named 'Gia Thạnh đường' by Emperor Gia Long in 1808. A national architectural-art relic (1993): a five-bay timber-frame đình with tube-tiled roof, 'two dragons contesting the pearl' friezes and Ông Nhật–Bà Nguyệt statuary — a rare monument to how the Minh Hương wove into Vietnamese culture.

places.n: Đền thờ Vua Hùng (Hung Kings Temple, Thao Cam Vien)
places.ad: 2 Nguyễn Bình Khiêm, Quận 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A near-century-old temple inside the Botanical Gardens, built by the French in 1926 as a 'Temple du souvenir' and rededicated after 1954 to the Hùng Kings and other national heroes. Modeled on Huế imperial-palace architecture with a 3-ton bronze elephant in the forecourt; the focal point of Saigon's Giỗ Tổ Hùng Vương observances each third lunar month.

places.n: Lăng Ông Thủy Tướng Cần Giờ (Whale Lord Shrine)
places.ad: Thị trấn Cần Thạnh, huyện Cần Giờ, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A Nguyễn-era coastal shrine to Cá Ông (the whale deity revered by fishermen), at the end of Duyên Hải road in Cần Thạnh — and home to a 12 m whale skeleton. Its Nghinh Ông 'Sea Tết' festival, held since 1913 on the 15th of the eighth lunar month, is one of only three National Intangible Cultural Heritages of Ho Chi Minh City.

places.n: Khách sạn Grand Sài Gòn (Hotel Grand Saigon)
places.ad: 8 Đồng Khởi, Quận 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: One of Saigon's three great heritage hotels (with the Continental and Majestic), opened 1930 at 8 rue Catinat with classical French lines — and still running its original 1930 cage elevator. A near-century of Đồng Khởi history preserved in the 'ancient wing'; step into the lobby or the rooftop bar to feel old Saigon.

places.n: Trường THPT chuyên Lê Hồng Phong (Lycée Petrus Ký)
places.ad: 235 Nguyễn Văn Cừ, Quận 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The former Lycée Petrus Trương Vĩnh Ký, built 1927 on an 8-ha campus in classical French style — the leading boys' lycée of the colonial south and still an elite specialist school. Ranked among the city's top-10 architectural-art heritage sites (2015); its ochre halls and old courtyards are a quiet architecture stop in Chợ Lớn's fringe.

places.n: Trường THPT Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai (Trường Áo Tím / Gia Long)
places.ad: 275 Điện Biên Phủ, Quận 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The 1913 Collège des Jeunes Filles Indigènes — the storied girls' school known first as the 'Purple Áo Dài School', then Gia Long — a Gothic-influenced early-20th-century complex on a 23,000 m² block. A century of southern women's education; ranked a city Architectural-Art Monument in 2012.

places.ad: 159 Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa, Quận 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A 1918 girls' lycée on a rare four-frontage block, built in Indochine style (yellow walls, red tile, high arched gates) and one of the very few century-old schools in Vietnam still under its original name. Ranked a city heritage site (2015); it still keeps 100-year-old xà cừ trees, a wooden staircase and water tank.

places.ad: Nối Quận 7 với TP. Thủ Đức (sông Sài Gòn), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The largest cable-stayed bridge in the city — a 2,000 m span (705 m cable-stayed) opened September 2009 on the Ring Road 2, linking Phú Mỹ Hưng in District 7 to the Thủ Thiêm side. A modern engineering icon of Saigon, photogenic from the riverside at dusk.

places.n: Kênh Nhiêu Lộc - Thị Nghè (Nhieu Loc Canal)
places.ad: Chạy qua Quận 1, Quận 3, Phú Nhuận, Bình Thạnh, Tân Bình, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A nearly 10 km 'green ribbon' through the inner city — once a dead, polluted canal, reborn after a decade-long clean-up into landscaped embankments and a signature of Saigon's revival. Since 2015 a 4.5 km guided boat tour (covered wooden boats and hand-rowed phụng boats) runs it with đờn ca tài tử music; the multi-coloured bridge lighting is a night check-in.

places.n: Đình Thông Tây Hội (Thong Tay Hoi Communal House)
places.ad: Đường Thống Nhất, phường 11, Quận Gò Vấp, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The oldest surviving đình (village communal house) in all of southern Vietnam — first raised in 1679 by Nghệ An migrants and rebuilt in 1883 in the layered 'trùng thiềm điệp ốc' style, honouring two 11th-century Lý princes. A national Architectural-Art-Historical Monument since 1998, prized for its intricate dragon-phoenix woodcarving.

places.n: Địa đạo Phú Thọ Hòa (Phu Tho Hoa Tunnels)
places.ad: 139 Phú Thọ Hòa, phường Phú Thọ Hòa, Quận Tân Phú, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A resistance-era tunnel network right inside the city — dug from the 1940s and used to stage raids on Tân Sơn Nhất airfield and the Bảy Hiền/Phú Thọ Hòa depots. Recognised a national historical site in 1996 and the only one in Tân Phú District; a compact, little-visited alternative to the Củ Chi tunnels.

places.ad: Phường Phú Mỹ, Bà Rịa - Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
places.w: A ~500 m pilgrimage mountain on the way to Vũng Tàu, threaded with over 100 temples and cave-hermitages hidden in its granite — Tổ Đình Linh Sơn, Hang Tổ, Hang Mai, Chùa Diệu Linh and more — plus streams and viewpoints. A national historical site (1993) and a favourite spiritual-and-adventure day hike east of the city.

places.n: Nhà tù Côn Đảo & Nghĩa trang Hàng Dương
places.ad: Đặc khu Côn Đảo, Bà Rịa - Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
places.w: The 'hell on earth' prison archipelago — 113 years of French and American incarceration of Vietnamese patriots, its tiger cages, cell blocks and the Côn Đảo Museum ranked a Special National Monument (2012, 17 component sites). Hàng Dương cemetery (20 ha, 1,900+ graves incl. heroine Võ Thị Sáu) is a candle-lit pilgrimage. An overnight boat/flight trip; also known for pristine beaches and sea-turtle nesting.

places.ad: 28 Vo Van Tan Street, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: HCMC's unflinching museum of the Indochina and Vietnam wars — the city's most affecting historical site.

places.ad: Le Loi, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The landmark 1914 central market — street food, textiles and souvenirs in the heart of Saigon.

places.ad: Cu Chi District (Ben Dinh / Ben Duoc), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The vast wartime underground tunnel network northwest of the city — a defining day trip from Saigon.

places.ad: 288 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia (in the alley), Vo Thi Sau Ward, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Legendary 60-year alley phở serving strict Nam Dinh/Northern-style beef phở with no herbs, sprouts or hoisin - the 'take it or leave it' bowl locals queue for.

places.ad: 435 Ly Thai To, Ward 9, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: North-to-South phở institution since 1954, famed for its giant 'to xe lua' (train-car) bowl of simple, garnish-free Northern phở bac that Saigonese have loved for 70+ years.

places.ad: 25 Mac Dinh Chi, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: One of Saigon's oldest phở houses, founded 1947 by Mr Tran Van Phon and still simmering its crystal-clear, lightly sweet broth over a charcoal stove; now second/third generation.

places.ad: 380 Nguyen Tri Phuong, Ward 6, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The standout of District 10's neon-lit chè Thái street; a famously rich Thai-style sweet soup of pureed durian, jackfruit, palm seed and longan in coconut milk.

places.ad: Vo Van Tan, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: One of Saigon's most storied hủ tiếu Nam Vang brands and reputedly its most expensive bowl - Chinese-Cambodian noodles with minced pork, liver, heart, shrimp and quail egg in a refined sweet broth.

places.ad: 113A Dang Dung, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The 'Commando Cafe' - a 1940s house that was a secret Viet Cong special-forces base with a weapons bunker and hidden mailbox; today it pours nostalgic bac xiu and serves com tam Dai Han above its wartime tunnel.

places.ad: 207B Nguyen Van Thu, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A perennially packed bún bò Huế spot beside the Conservatory of Music, singled out by a visiting New York chef as one of the best bowls of soup in all of Vietnam.

places.n: Banh Khot Co Ba Vung Tau
places.ad: 40B Tran Cao Van, Ward 6, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Saigon's best-known outpost of Vung Tau-style banh khot - crispy coconut-batter mini rice pancakes topped with shrimp - wrapped with herbs and dipped in sweet fish sauce; also serves banh xeo.

places.ad: 277 Vo Van Tan, Ward 5, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A 40-year Chinese-Vietnamese street stall whose bot chien - rice-flour cake pan-fried crisp in a copper pan with egg, scallion and rich soy - is a Saigon late-afternoon institution.

places.ad: 25 Hoang Sa, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Canalside beef pho stall; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand 2024-2026, famed for its long-braised oxtail.

places.ad: 63/6 Pasteur, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Alley pho institution serving Saigonese since 1945; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand, pairs its broth with pate chaud.

places.ad: 260C Pasteur, Ward 8, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Landmark Southern pho since 1968; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand, a whole plate of herbs, bean sprouts and you tiao.

places.ad: 413-415 Nguyen Trai, Ward 7, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Cholon-area pho household name since 1970; generous flank-and-filet bowls, in the MICHELIN Guide selection.

places.ad: 460 Nguyen Tri Phuong, Ward 9, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: MICHELIN Bib Gourmand pho whose owner simmers a clear beef broth over 12 hours; customizable cuts.

places.ad: 148 Vo Thi Sau, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Humble pho ga stall since 1958 in the MICHELIN Guide; freshly-made clear chicken broth, second generation.

places.ad: 19 Huynh Khuong Ninh, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Nearly-century-old banh mi cart (est. 1930), now third generation, with homemade pate and pork roll.

places.ad: 53 Cao Thang, Ward 3, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Iconic 1958 breakfast spot; sizzling cast-iron skillet of fried eggs, pate and cold cuts with baguette.

places.ad: 37-39 Nguyen Trai, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Alley cart open ~4 hours a day; sweet charcoal-grilled pork patties in place of pate, a Saigon street icon.

places.ad: Vo Van Tan, Ban Co Ward, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Chinese-Khmer-Vietnamese hu tieu Nam Vang since 1975; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand celebrated for its Phnom Penh-style bowl.

places.ad: 89 Ton That Dam, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Chef Peter Cuong Franklin's MICHELIN-starred restaurant over the Ton That Dam market; street food reimagined as fine dining.

places.ad: 136/9 Le Thanh Ton (Hem 136), Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Hole-in-the-wall down an alley by Ben Thanh's north gate; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand home cooking and shrimp banh xeo.

places.ad: 127 Dinh Tien Hoang, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: MICHELIN Bib Gourmand banh cuon shop; freshly-made, paper-thin steamed rolls with pork and mushroom.

places.n: Banh Canh Cua 87 Tran Khac Chan
places.ad: 87 Tran Khac Chan, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Corner stall famed for a thick, stew-like crab banh canh loaded with crab meat, crab cake and quail egg.

places.ad: 212B Alley, Nguyen Trai, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Saigon's most famous snail operation tucked down a downtown alley; 100+ snail and shellfish dishes.

places.ad: 42 Nguyen Hue, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: 1960s apartment block on the Nguyen Hue walking street turned vertical warren of 50+ cafes; a Saigon coffee landmark.

places.ad: 27 Ngo Duc Ke (2nd floor), Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Saigon's pioneering specialty-coffee roaster in a 1912 building; pour-over, cold brew and light-roast Arabica.

places.ad: 109/36 Nguyen Thien Thuat, Ward 2, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Saigon's oldest cafe (est. 1938), sole keeper of ca phe vot cloth-filter coffee, run by the founder's daughters.

places.ad: Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (corner by Ben Thanh Market)
places.w: Nearly-70-year sticky-rice corner by Ben Thanh Market; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand xoi ga with house pate and quail egg.

places.ad: 10 Dang Tat, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Beloved home-cooking restaurant in restored villas; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand, rice cooked in cast iron on wood stoves.

places.ad: 67 Ton That Dam, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Cantonese clay-pot rice shop since 1948, now third generation; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand for its double-boiled silkie soup.

places.ad: 129/4 Vo Van Tan, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Alley hideaway with a rooftop balcony; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand home cooking, signature oyster-and-beef hotpot.

places.ad: 15/20 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Owner-run shop of generous Hanoian home cooking; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand bun rieu cua topped with crispy fried tofu.

places.ad: 55 Dong Du, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Always-busy Cantonese dim sum house by the Dong Du mosque; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand, a large dim sum and BBQ selection.

places.ad: 59 Ho Xuan Huong, Ward 6, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Bourdain's 'flying rice': clay pots smashed and rice tossed across the room, from A Cook's Tour and No Reservations.

places.ad: 36 Le Loi (5th floor), Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Hidden rooftop above Le Loi serving northern Vietnamese home cooking with city views; part of the Cuc Gach/Secret Garden family.

places.ad: 167-169 Calmette, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Marou's flagship cafe and bean-to-bar chocolate factory in a heritage building; award-winning single-origin Vietnamese cacao.

places.ad: 23 Hoang Sa, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Nguyen Thi Thanh's canalside stall made famous by Bourdain's No Reservations; a different regional noodle soup each day.

places.ad: 136 Le Thanh Ton (1st floor), Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: 1960s-70s-styled cocktail bar on Asia's 50 Best Bars list; local-ingredient drinks like the sugarcane Nuoc Mia Highball.

places.ad: 25 Ho Tung Mau (2nd floor), Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Ingredient-focused hidden cocktail bar; debuted on Asia's 50 Best Bars (No.99, 2024) with drinks built on Vietnamese produce.

places.ad: 17-19 Ngo Van Nam, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Well-loved modern-traditional Vietnamese restaurant (since 2011); MSG-free home dishes in a vintage-contemporary setting.

places.ad: 110 Suong Nguyet Anh, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: MICHELIN Bib Gourmand modern-Vietnamese vegan kitchen using produce from the family garden; punchy bun Vi Que broth.

places.n: Sủi Cảo Hà Tôn Quyền (Thiên Thiên)
places.ad: Hà Tôn Quyền, Ward 4, District 11, Cholon, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The heart of Saigon's nicknamed 'phố sủi cảo' — a cluster of Hoa family dumpling shops (Thiên Thiên among the best-known) that have run for 30+ years each. Plump shrimp-and-pork sủi cảo steamed, fried, or in clear soup with handmade noodles.

places.ad: Trần Hưng Đạo B, Ward 11, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: An ~80-year-old Cantonese dessert cart (opened 1938 by a Guangdong immigrant), nicknamed Chè Cột Điện and Chè Ma for its lamppost spot and late hours. Warm and iced Chinese sweet soups — almond, black-sesame, lotus and herbal chè — done the old way.

places.ad: Châu Văn Liêm, Ward 11, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A Chợ Lớn dumpling stalwart on Châu Văn Liêm known for chive-packed sủi cảo — soft-yet-chewy dumplings loaded with garlic-chive; also plates a Chinese-style phá lấu. A neighbourhood authority on the craft.

places.ad: 274/29 Võ Văn Tần, Ward 5, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Family-run bún bò Huế in a narrow District 3 alley; a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand for its rich lemongrass-and-beef-bone broth and generous mixed bowl.

places.ad: Nguyễn Thượng Hiền (Điện Biên Phủ to Nguyễn Đình Chiểu), Bàn Cờ Ward, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: District 3's official night food street (opened Dec 2022) on a stretch Time Out ranked among the world's coolest; ~90 stalls of bánh tráng trộn, snails and skewers, 7pm–11pm.

places.ad: Hồ Thị Kỷ, Ward 1, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A 300m alley market settled by Vietnamese-Cambodian refugees in the 1970s, now Saigon's densest Cambodian-Vietnamese food alley (100+ stalls); Khmer fish noodles, prahok and palm-sugar chè, from ~3pm.

places.ad: 116/2/3 Phan Đăng Lưu, Ward 3, Phú Nhuận, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A 40-year alley institution off Phan Đăng Lưu famous for warm bánh đúc ladled to order with pork, wood-ear mushroom and fried shallots; once notorious for its brusque service.

places.ad: 2 Lam Son Square (Park Hyatt Saigon), Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Park Hyatt Saigon's martini bar and one of the city's cocktail landmarks, running guest shifts with bartenders drawn from the World's Best Bars.

places.ad: Caravelle Saigon, 19-23 Lam Son Square, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Historic 10th-floor rooftop bar atop the Caravelle Hotel, a wartime haunt of diplomats and correspondents since 1959, with live music and skyline views.

places.ad: 38 Nguyễn Ư Dĩ, Thảo Điền, Thủ Đức City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Saigon's benchmark riverside restaurant-bar (since 2008) on a near-rural stretch of the Saigon River; named by The Guardian among the world's best bars, and Rusty Compass's pick for the city's best riverside meal.

places.ad: Ngô Quang Huy, Thảo Điền, Thủ Đức City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Chef-owner Thierry Mounon's elegant colonial villa off Thảo Điền serving classic French gastronomy from the southwest; a MICHELIN Selected restaurant (2023 & 2024) with a deep French wine list.

places.ad: 4F, The Reverie Saigon, 22-36 Nguyen Hue, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: One MICHELIN Star; chef Angus Chan's refined Cantonese kitchen inside The Reverie, weaving Vietnamese ingredients into Hong Kong technique amid jade and gold-leaf interiors.

places.ad: District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A 30-year Cholon institution that grew from a single chè stall into a symbol of Chinese-Vietnamese sweets — egg-in-tea chè and almond chè among the classics.

places.ad: 534 Vĩnh Khánh, District 4, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: The most famous ốc house on District 4's Vĩnh Khánh seafood strip (~20 years); a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand 2024 pick, signature salt-roasted crab claws, plastic-stool buzz.

places.ad: 22 Đặng Hữu Phổ, Thảo Điền, District 2 (Thủ Đức City), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A tranquil green villa in Thảo Điền serving authentic Vietnamese with a gentle modern twist and vegetarian focus — a District 2 expat favourite.

places.ad: Thảo Điền, District 2, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (also Lê Lợi & Đồng Khởi, District 1)
places.w: A pioneering concept-store cafe-bistro brand that keeps innovating brunch with Vietnamese ingredients; the Thảo Điền outlet anchors District 2.

places.ad: 27 Lưu Văn Lang, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Widely regarded as one of the city's best practitioners of specialty coffee — serious brew hardware, Vietnamese and international beans, standout egg coffee.

places.ad: 26 Lý Tự Trọng & Nguyễn Huệ, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (multiple branches)
places.w: The retro, olive-green subsidy-era chain that made cà phê cốt dừa (coconut coffee) a Saigon signature — a near-obligatory coconut-coffee stop.

places.ad: 22 Lê Lợi, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (branches incl. Thảo Điền, District 2)
places.w: A sleek retro-Saigon small-batch roaster near Bến Thành that blends traditional Vietnamese coffee with modern specialty craft across its city outlets.

places.ad: Saigon Pearl, Nguyễn Hữu Cảnh, Bình Thạnh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A multi-storey riverside coffee mansion (opened 2016) that helped awaken Vietnam's Arabica specialty scene and trained national barista champions.

places.ad: 1st floor, 136 Lê Thánh Tôn, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Saigon's highest-placed bar on Asia's 50 Best Bars (ranked 2022-2025, No. 61 in 2025) — a speakeasy-jazz room of precise modern-classic drinks.

places.ad: District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Layla's experimental sibling and a sustainability-driven cocktail lab — Saigon's sole entrant on Asia's 50 Best Bars 51-100 in 2021 (No. 77).

places.ad: 1st floor, 14 Tôn Thất Đạm, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A 1920s New York-styled speakeasy specialising in classic cocktails and mixology — one of the bars that seeded Saigon's speakeasy wave.

places.ad: 26 Le Thi Rieng Street, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: Saigon's most famous banh mi since 1989 — permanent queues for the thap cam loaded with pate and cold cuts.

places.ad: 84 Dang Van Ngu Street, Phu Nhuan District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
places.w: A Bib Gourmand com tam house famous for its thick, well-charred grilled pork chop over broken rice.
